issues.detail: The Hebrew says 'Bathsheba daughter of Eliam' (בַּת שֶׁ֣בַע בַּת אֱלִיעָ֔ם), but the Chinese renders '以利暗人的女兒巴特施罷' — '以利暗人' appears to be a misreading/transposition of '以利暗' (Eliam) plus an extraneous 人, and '巴特施罷' is an odd rendering of Bathsheba (בַּת שֶׁבַע) that could confuse the name; more importantly, the Hebrew explicitly names her 'Bathsheba daughter of Eliam', while the Chinese says 'the daughter of the Eliamite' (以利暗人的女兒), which changes the proper name 'Eliam' into a gentilic and drops the name 'Bathsheba' as a proper name, replacing it with a transliteration that is not standard. This is a name fidelity issue.
